problem:
Let $⟨-1,y⟩$ be the solution of the system of equations below. 

$$
{\begin{aligned}2x+ky=-4 \\ 3x-4y=5.\end{aligned}
$$

Which of the following equations could be solved to find the value of $k?$

- $|\begin{aligned}2 & k \\ 3 & -4\end{aligned}|=-2|\begin{aligned}-4 & k \\ 5 & -4\end{aligned}|$
- $|\begin{aligned}2 & k \\ 3 & -4\end{aligned}|=|\begin{aligned}-4 & k \\ 5 & -4\end{aligned}|$
- $|\begin{aligned}2 & k \\ 3 & -4\end{aligned}|=-|\begin{aligned}-4 & k \\ 5 & -4\end{aligned}|$

examples.problem:
Let $\langle x,3 \rangle$ be the solution of the system of equations below. 

$$
{\begin{aligned}5x-2y=4 \\ x+ky=8\end{aligned}
$$

Which of the following equations could be solved to find the value of $k?$

- ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14059292/assets/a404c14afc5aeda319edcad04d7ea6f7f9ee0631f3a86c567a48f448dc21de8e.png)

- ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14059292/assets/648ce0c1b8b77c1230c6c634c676624f9c79c12ffc3942abc09d24d0fdc424d3.png)

- ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14059292/assets/f23784cb494ee42a65b07597b9f287b107b81502fba3a51b22344d804ee937a8.png)
examples.worked_solution:
The determinant of the coefficient matrix is

$$
\begin{aligned}D & =|\begin{aligned}5 & -2 \\ 1 & k\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

According to Cramer's rule, the value of $y$ is given by $y=\dfrac{D_y}{D},$ where

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{y} & =|\begin{aligned}5 & 4 \\ 1 & 8\end{aligned}| \\  & =5\cdot 8-4\cdot 1 \\  & =36.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\frac{{D}_{y}}{D} \\ 3 & =\frac{36}{|\begin{aligned}5 & -2 \\ 1 & k\end{aligned}|} \\ |\begin{aligned}5 & -2 \\ 1 & k\end{aligned}| & =12\end{aligned}
$$

So, the correct answer is "II only".

feedback.worked_solution:
We are given the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}4x+7y=13 \\ -2x+5y=19.\end{aligned}
$$

The determinant of the coefficient matrix is

$$
\begin{aligned}D & =|\begin{aligned}4 & 7 \\ -2 & 5\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to construct ${D}_{y}$ we replace the second column of the coefficient matrix by the right-hand side column of the given system:

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{y} & =|\begin{aligned}4 & 13 \\ -2 & 19\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, according to Cramer's rule, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\frac{{D}_{y}}{D}=\frac{|\begin{aligned}4 & 13 \\ -2 & 19\end{aligned}|}{|\begin{aligned}4 & 7 \\ -2 & 5\end{aligned}|}.\end{aligned}
$$
